record.paper_title: Projection Algorithms: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: inconsistent cyclic projections for three or more sets
record.original_question: For cyclic projections onto three or more closed convex sets whose intersection is empty, what is the asymptotic behavior of the projection sequence? More specifically, is there an analogue for the N-set inconsistent case of the two-set dichotomy described in Fact 4.1, including an appropriate replacement for the displacement vector v that governs the behavior of alternating projections for two sets?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. What is the behavior of the sequence of cyclic projections for three or more sets with empty intersection?

The crux of the problem is this: the vector v in Fact 4.1 is well-defined and important for the formulation of the behavior of the sequence of alternating projections even when the distance d(C1; C2) = inf{||c1 - c2|| : c1 in C1; c2 in C2} is not attained, i.e., v 62 C2 - C1; however, it is not known how to define the vector(s) analogous to v in the N-set case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space and let $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_N \subseteq H$ (with $N \ge 3$) be closed convex sets such that $\bigcap_{i=1}^N C_i = \emptyset$. For each $i$, denote by $P_i \colon H \to C_i$ the metric projection onto $C_i$, and consider the cyclic projection operator
$$T \;=\; P_N \circ P_{N-1} \circ \cdots \circ P_1.$$
For any starting point $x_0 \in H$, define the sequence $x_{k+1} = T(x_k)$.

For $N = 2$, the asymptotic behavior is described by the following dichotomy. Let
$$v \;\in\; \overline{C_2 - C_1}$$
be the unique element of minimum norm (the displacement vector); equivalently $v$ is the projection of $0$ onto the closed convex set $\overline{C_2 - C_1}$. Then either
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] the distance $d(C_1, C_2) = \inf\{\|c_1 - c_2\| : c_1 \in C_1, c_2 \in C_2\}$ is attained and the alternating projection sequence converges (weakly or strongly under standard hypotheses) to a fixed point of $P_1 \circ P_2$, or
  \item[(ii)] the distance is not attained, $v \notin C_2 - C_1$, and $\|x_k\| \to \infty$ in a manner controlled by $v$, with $x_{k+1} - x_k \to -v$.
\end{enumerate}

Problem. Describe the asymptotic behavior of the cyclic projection sequence $(x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ in the inconsistent $N$-set case ($N \ge 3$). In particular, formulate and prove an analogue of the above two-set dichotomy that includes an appropriate replacement for the displacement vector $v$ governing the behavior of $(x_k)$, valid even when the natural infimal distances among the sets $C_1, \ldots, C_N$ are not attained.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is known. Bauschke established asymptotic regularity of the cyclic composition $T$ (the "zero displacement conjecture"), showing $x_{k+1}-x_k \to 0$ along arbitrarily small displacements, and subsequent work by Bauschke, Borwein, Lewis and others studied difference vectors for compositions of projections in the inconsistent case. However, a complete $N$-set analogue of the two-set dichotomy with an intrinsic displacement vector governing the behavior of the cyclic sequence (especially when relevant infima are not attained) is not established in full generality, and the problem is still considered open in the broader literature.

status_evidence.title: Compositions of projection mappings: fixed point sets and difference vectors
status_evidence.snippet: Bauschke, Borwein and Lewis systematically studied compositions of projections in the inconsistent case for closed convex nonempty sets C_1,...,C_n in a real Hilbert space; the displacement vector is defined as the projection of 0 onto the closure of an appropriate Minkowski difference.
status_evidence.claim: Difference/displacement vectors for cyclic compositions have been partially characterized, but a complete analogue of the two-set dichotomy is not given.

status_evidence.title: The composition of projections onto closed convex sets in Hilbert space is asymptotically regular
status_evidence.snippet: Bauschke proved asymptotic regularity of the composition of projections (zero displacement conjecture).
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic regularity is established, providing partial results toward describing the asymptotic behavior.

status_evidence.title: The method of cyclic projections for closed convex sets in a Hilbert space under the presence of computational errors
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the inconsistent cyclic projection method and approximate solutions, indicating the asymptotic behavior remains a subject of ongoing study.
status_evidence.claim: The inconsistent N-set case is still actively investigated.
